body:
Pushing an ascription all the way through a value (`Ascriptions.transition_multiple`) rebuilt the value, every list cell and tuple field, even when nothing inside changed. A well-typed list crossing a typed parameter, `fun rows : [Row] -> ...`, was copied whole on every call. It costs time and garbage, and the copies are new objects, which defeats anything that keeps values by identity. It's also invisible to a step count: the whole copy is one `Ascription` step.

## What changes

- The list, cons, tuple, label and constructor-payload cases of `Ascriptions.transition` now build a new node only when one of its parts came back different. Otherwise they return the value itself. Plain data that already has the type crosses a typed boundary as the same objects, keeping its ids, as the file's header asks.
- A value that holds a function is still wrapped, as before.
- Only the recursive push can give a part back unchanged. The stepwise push wraps each part in a new ascription, so it behaves as before.
- The `Parens` case, which its comment calls impossible, now passes its value on rather than a fresh copy, for the same reason.

## Measured

`hazel bench-eval`, 15 runs each, A/B/A on one machine:

| Program | With the change | `dev` | With the change, again |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A list of 2,000 labeled tuples passed 30 times through a typed parameter | 269 ms | 382 ms | 267 ms |
| `bench/eval-bench.hz` (recursion, lists, matches) | 764 ms | 764 ms | 749 ms |

The first is about 30% faster; the benchmark of ordinary code is unchanged.

On the livelits integration branch (#2635), the same change made the Scenes slide's picture view (about 570 shapes) 20–25% faster: about 725–830 ms became 520–650 ms. That's because each crossing of `view_box(pic : Picture)` and friends had copied 15,500 nodes. It also let the view's call memo keep its keys cheap.

## Testing

- `Test_Ascriptions` adds two tests. A well-typed list of labeled tuples, given its type, comes back as the same object; that test fails on `dev`. A list holding a function still comes back as a new value.
- The Ascriptions, Evaluator, Elaboration, Stepper, Probe, ObsBench, WorkerServer and Statics groups pass: 967 tests.
- `dune fmt` is clean.
